title: bug: launcher suites beyond postflight/worktree-landing still hit MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE when run from a task worktree
description:
Follow-up to task-3c4be125.

That row gives postflight.{sh,ps1} and worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} the harness-only seam MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER=1. Only the exact value '1' skips WT-13's MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE refusal.

Other launcher suites also launch their own checkout's scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}. Run from a task worktree W, they are still refused. Candidates found while planning task-3c4be125; verify each one first:
- agent-git-guard.test.mjs: launches path.join(scripts,'moe-agent.sh'|'.ps1'). Its `clean` env strips MOE_*.
- protected-agent-command.test.mjs: SH/PS1 = ../moe-agent.*. Its env strips MOE_|CLAUDE|FAKE_.
- agent-runtime.test.mjs: runs `moe-agent.sh --help`, and the guard fires before --help. It inherits process.env.
- wave1-pilot.mjs: launches REPO/scripts/moe-agent.*.
- mention-provenance.{sh,ps1}: WRAPPER=$ROOT_DIR/scripts/moe-agent.sh.
- worktree-e2e.cjs (WT-19b's file): launches its wrapper argument, and its `inherited` strips MOE_*. WT-19's step-6 full-regression command runs it, so WT-19 cannot verify from W without this fix.
- Also check usage-attribution.test.mjs and moe-account-lease.test.mjs. Suites that only extract wrapper functions never reach the guard.

Impact: any post-switch row that verifies with these suites cannot pass from its worktree until this lands. That includes WT-19 and the agent-git-guard and protected-runtime bug rows.

Also in scope:
- Register MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER in the env-name lists of parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1.
- List it as a test seam in docs/CONFIGURATION.md, beside MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF. WT-17 and WT-19 also declare that doc, so coordinate with them.

Constraints:
- Every guard-refusal case stays seam-free.
- Split the row if it goes over the file cap.
definitionOfDone: Each candidate suite that launches the full wrapper sets MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER='1' for the wrapper copies it launches. Every candidate that does not launch it is named in the summary with the reason.

Each changed suite passes when run from a copy of scripts/ at <scratch git repo>/.worktrees/task-x/, plus whatever other inputs that suite reads. The same copy without this change fails with [ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:. The summary records the exact commands.
Every case that tests the guard's refusal still launches without the seam and still sees the refusal.
parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 list the env name, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.
git grep finds the env name only in scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}, scripts/tests/** and docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

- Kill only PIDs you recorded (mem:gotcha-qa-windows-launcher-tests-from-wsl).

C1, the DoD 4 and DoD 5 checks (fast):

C2, the GREEN bash leg (the complete_task verification):
T=scripts/tests;U=$(env|awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ",$1}');X=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/86431c31.XXXXXX")&&G="git -C $X/r"&&mkdir $X/r $X/pw&&git archive HEAD|tar -x -C $X/r&&cp --parents $T/{agent-git-guard.test.mjs,protected-agent-command.test.mjs,mention-provenance.sh,mention-provenance.ps1,worktree-e2e.cjs,wave1-pilot.mjs,parity-check.sh,parity-check.ps1} docs/CONFIGURATION.md $X/r&&cp $T/postflight-fake-proxy.js $X/fp.js&&$G init -q&&$G add -A&&$G -c user.name=g -c user.email=g@g.invalid commit -qm t&&$G worktree add -q --detach .worktrees/task-x&&cd $X/r/.worktrees/task-x&&env $U node --test $T/{agent-git-guard,protected-agent-command,agent-runtime}.test.mjs&&env $U bash $T/mention-provenance.sh&&env $U node $T/worktree-e2e.cjs sh scripts/moe-agent.sh $X/fp.js $X bash&&env $U MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-guard node $T/postflight-worktree.cjs sh $PWD/scripts/moe-agent.sh $X/fp.js $X/pw bash&&bash $T/parity-check.sh
- It copies W's tree (HEAD plus this row's nine files) into a fresh scratch repo and registers <scratch repo>/.worktrees/task-x. That is a real task worktree, so WT-13's guard applies to every wrapper launched from it.
- From there, all of these must pass:

  - agent-runtime, unchanged, which proves it needs no seam;
  - mention-provenance.sh, which prints PASSED;

C3, the RED bash leg:
N=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER;T=scripts/tests;S="$T/agent-git-guard.test.mjs $T/protected-agent-command.test.mjs $T/mention-provenance.sh $T/worktree-e2e.cjs";U=$(env|awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ",$1}')&&X=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/86431c31-red.XXXXXX")&&mkdir $X/r&&git archive HEAD|tar -x -C $X/r&&cp --parents $S $X/r&&(cd $X/r&&sed -i "/$N/d" $S)&&cp $T/postflight-fake-proxy.js $X/fp.js&&git -C $X/r init -q&&git -C $X/r add -A&&git -C $X/r -c user.name=g -c user.email=g@g.invalid commit -qm t&&git -C $X/r worktree add -q --detach .worktrees/task-x&&cd $X/r/.worktrees/task-x||exit 1;r(){ env $U "$@">$X/r.log 2>&1&&return 1;grep -qE '\[ERROR\] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:|codes=MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE' $X/r.log;};r node --test $T/agent-git-guard.test.mjs&&r node --test $T/protected-agent-command.test.mjs&&r bash $T/mention-provenance.sh&&r node $T/worktree-e2e.cjs sh scripts/moe-agent.sh $X/fp.js $X bash&&echo "RED ok: all 4 suites refused without the seam"

- Each of the four suites must fail, and its output must carry the refusal: `[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:`, or `codes=MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE` for agent-git-guard, which prints only the codes it saw.
- It ends with `RED ok: all 4 suites refused without the seam`.

C4, the PS leg (Windows node and PowerShell, run through WSL interop):
N=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER;T=scripts/tests;Q="pwsh.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\\tests\\mention-provenance.ps1 -PowerShell";X=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/86431c31-ps.XXXXXX)||exit 1;for c in g r;do W=$X/$c/.worktrees/task-x;mkdir -p $W&&git -C $X/$c init -q&&git archive HEAD|tar -x -C $W&&cp --parents $T/{mention-provenance.ps1,wave1-pilot.mjs} $W&&{ [ $c = g ]||(cd $W&&sed -i "/$N/d" $T/mention-provenance.ps1 $T/wave1-pilot.mjs);}||exit 1;for p in moe-daemon moe-proxy;do cmd.exe /c mklink /J "$(wslpath -w $W/packages/$p/node_modules)" "D:\\projexts\\moes\\packages\\$p\\node_modules">/dev/null||exit 1;done;done;cd $X/g/.worktrees/task-x&&$Q powershell&&$Q pwsh&&node.exe $T/wave1-pilot.mjs&&cd $X/r/.worktrees/task-x&&! $Q powershell>$X/m.log 2>&1&&grep -qF '[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:' $X/m.log&&! node.exe $T/wave1-pilot.mjs>$X/p.log 2>&1&&grep -qF '[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:' $X/p.log&&echo "PS leg ok: green passed, red refused"
- Windows git cannot follow a WSL-made worktree link. So here the copy is a plain directory at <scratch repo>/.worktrees/task-x/ inside a WSL-made repo on D:. The guard's prefix rule refuses that copy too (probed).
- The packages' node_modules are junctioned, read-only, to the control checkout's, as wave1-pilot's header asks (mem:gotcha-wave1-pilot-and-git-bash-spawn).
- GREEN:
  - mention-provenance.ps1 prints PASSED with the PS 5.1 child (`-PowerShell powershell`) and with pwsh;
  - wave1-pilot prints `PASS: Wave 1 pilot success path, 27 links` (pwsh wrapper).
- RED, from the copy with the seam lines deleted: both fail with `[ERROR] MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE:`.
- The parent is pwsh on purpose. Under a Windows PowerShell 5.1 parent, mention-provenance.ps1 fails its child-host probe before any wrapper launch, and it does so at HEAD too. That pre-existing harness bug is filed as task-e856c24678e94ff4b38ef79c99069e24; it is not this row's.
- wave1-pilot must run on Windows node. Under WSL, the Windows-installed node_modules cannot resolve TypeScript's native linux binary.
- After C4, unlink its four junctions from WSL with a plain `rm <link>`. Never use `rm -r` through them, and never a Windows recursive delete. Then check that D:\projexts\moes\packages\moe-daemon\node_modules and moe-proxy\node_modules still list entries (mem:gotcha-worktree-node-modules-junction).

Expected: all four exit 0.
- If a suite fails for a reason other than the seam, attribute it before any retry, and never weaken a suite. Examples: an unrelated landed change, or a missing input such as Windows python.
- If the failure is not yours, report_blocked with the evidence.

error handling: every command is an && chain, so it fails closed.
- A scratch-setup failure (mktemp, archive, git init, worktree add, mklink) exits non-zero before any suite runs.
- C3's `r` helper fails both when a suite passes and when the refusal text is missing.
- The bash legs run every suite under `env $U`, and WSL interop forwards no MOE_* to the Windows processes. So an inherited seam can neither fake a pass nor mask a RED.

5. Adversarial self-review, then complete_task. Load adversarial-self-review, then check:

(1) Run `git diff -U0 -- scripts/tests/{agent-git-guard.test.mjs,protected-agent-command.test.mjs,mention-provenance.sh,mention-provenance.ps1,worktree-e2e.cjs,wave1-pilot.mjs} | grep -E '^[-+][^-+]' | grep -v MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER`. It must print nothing: every changed suite line names the seam, and nothing else moved. That is what makes the copies C3 and C4 rebuild 'the same copy without this change'.

(2) `git diff --stat` lists exactly the nine files. scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}, postflight*.{sh,ps1,cjs}, worktree-landing.* and agent-runtime.test.mjs are untouched.

(3) No refusal case gained the seam: `git grep -n MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE -- scripts/tests` hits only postflight-worktree.cjs, and C2's wt-guard run passed (DoD 3).

(4) Concurrency: the seam lives only in each suite's own child-process env. The ps1 suite restores it in finally, and no suite exports it to its caller. A parallel run, a peer harness or a live seat is therefore unaffected.

(5) Odd values: the suites set exactly '1'. The wrappers' exact-'1' checks (3c4be125) are untouched.

(6) Size: about +12/-0 lines.

Then:
- If any bytes change, re-run C1-C4.
- Call complete_task with C2 as the verification (command, exitCode, outputTail).
- Report modifiedFiles as exactly the nine files.
- The summary must carry:
  (a) the classification from step 1: the six changed suites; agent-runtime.test.mjs, unchanged, with its reason; each source-only suite with its reason; and acceptance.test.ts, out of scope;
  (b) step 1's RED;
  (c) C1, C3 and C4, each with its command, exit code and last lines.

This step adds no error handling of its own: any test failure loops back to step 4.

(a) Adding the seam to agent-runtime.test.mjs. Its fixture PATH has no git, so the guard never fires there, and with the seam added DoD 2's 'fails without this change' could never hold. It stays unchanged and is named in the summary.

planningNotes.risks:
DoD readings pinned here for QA:
(1) DoD 1/2: agent-runtime.test.mjs launches the wrapper but is never refused, because its PATH has no git. It stays unchanged and is named with that reason.
(2) DoD 2: 'changed suite' means the six launcher suites. parity-check.{sh,ps1} change only for DoD 4 and never launch the wrapper.
(3) DoD 5: the grep excludes the .moe/ board records, which are daemon-written task text that quotes the name.
(4) The 'without this change' copy is built by deleting the lines that name the env. By step 1's rule it is byte-identical to the pre-change file, which QA can check with step 5's git diff -U0.

Other risks:
- WT-19 also edits parity-check.* and CONFIGURATION.md. Adding new lines only keeps the hunks apart, but a true rebase conflict routes the task back under the epic's conflict policy.
- C4's junctions point at the control checkout's live node_modules. Unlink them with a plain rm only.
- If 3c4be125 reshaped the seam, follow the landed shape. Never edit the wrappers in this row.
